name: Baikal-GVD
summary: A growing deep-water neutrino telescope in Lake Baikal that uses independently operating clusters to search for high-energy cosmic neutrinos in the Northern Hemisphere.
detection_principle: Optical modules suspended on strings detect Cherenkov photons in freshwater. Each cluster contains a central string and surrounding strings, allowing reconstruction and expansion one cluster at a time.

sites.name: Baikal-GVD deep-water site
sites.location: Southern Lake Baikal, approximately 4 km offshore

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: The official site provides a 2026 sixteen-cluster configuration; expansion continues.

timeline.event: Evidence for a cosmic component in cascade events reported.

collaboration.name: Baikal Collaboration
lead_institutions: Institute for Nuclear Research, Russian Academy of Sciences
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: 2026 configuration
key_parameters.value: 16 clusters; approximately 0.8 km³ reported detector volume on the official project site

results.summary: Cascade data from 2018–2022 indicated an astrophysical component consistent with the flux observed by IceCube.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
